result.title: Teaching neural decoders with language
result.summary: Brain-computer interfaces decode neural activity, yet class-label supervision (CLS) leaves relationships among classes implicit. We propose Language as Supervision (LaS), which aligns neural features with natural-language class descriptions through learned projections and predicts classes using candidate text prototypes. We evaluate seven encoder architectures with independently trained models for visual, motor, and speech decoding from scalp and intracranial recordings. LaS improves speech-decoding accuracy by up to 17.15~pp over matched CLS baselines. Its representations support candidate-set reuse and label-supervised subject and session adaptation, while LaS enables conditional unseen-frequency decoding in steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) responses. Correct class-description correspondence supports this generalization, and dual-sided attribution visualization shows neural and textual contributions to the same class-matching score. These findings suggest that text descriptions can serve as general-purpose references for learning and interpretation in neural decoding.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Language as Supervision，用可学习投影把神经特征与自然语言类别描述对齐，并以候选文本原型完成分类，在视觉、运动、语音解码的七种编码器上验证，语音任务较标签监督基线最高提升 17.15 个百分点。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以文本原型作共享参考对齐内部表征、支持候选集复用与双面归因，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的语言监督与贡献分配提供可供核查的方法线索，但任务对象是脑信号解码，与多模态视觉推理距离较远。
